name: April 2018 Upper Midwest Blizzard

q.p: NWS Green Bay Area Forecast Discussion · long term, RDM
q.t: The system becomes a cutoff low Friday night, which then drifts towards the western Great Lakes Saturday and Sunday. The models have some differences in the rack of the system, so there is low confidence about the details of the forecast towards the end of the week.

q.p: NWS Green Bay Area Forecast Discussion · long term, RDM
q.t: Models continue to advertise the formation of a Front Range cyclone Thursday night, which moves towards Wisconsin Friday. The surface low is forecast to stay across southern Wisconsin. If it stays to the south we will have a cold rain or wet snow Thursday night and Friday with temperatures in the 30s or low 40s. If it moves further north we could have temperatures in the 50s in some areas.
THE GFS HAS TRENDED WEAKER AND FASTER IN THE LAST FEW RUNS AND FOCUSES THE ENERGY MORE TOWARD THE GREAT LAKES ON SATURDAY.
WPC KEPT OUR SNOWFALL AXIS GENERALLY IN THE MIDDLE OF THE MODEL SPREAD (NORTH OF THE GFS AND A BIT SOUTH OF THE ECMWF).
OVERALL WPC FAVORED THE SLOWER GUIDANCE, ECMWF AND UKMET, RATHER THAN THE SLIGHTLY MORE PROGRESSIVE SOLUTIONS, GFS AND NAM.
OVERALL WITH THE GFS BEING WARMER AND TRENDING COLDER...MORE WEIGHTING WAS GIVEN TO THE COLDER SREF/NAM/ECMWF FORECASTS.
THE NAM WAS COLDEST IN THE NEAR SURFACE LAYER WITH THE SREF MEAN NEXT COLDEST...WITH THE GFS WARMEST.
HOW FAR NORTH INTO MI LOW PRESSURE DEVELOPS WILL HELP DETERMINE THE NORTHWEST EXTENT OF HEAVY SNOW ON DAY 3 AS THE GFS/UKMET DO NOT EXTEND THE SNOW AXIS AS FAR WEST AS THE NAM/ECMWF/SREF MEAN.

q.p: NWS Green Bay Area Forecast Discussion
q.t: Last night into this morning, a 60 mile wide band of heavy snow occurred from Wausau to Marshfield to Wisconsin Rapids eastward to Green Bay, Oconto, Sturgeon Bay and Kewaunee. Snowfall totals in this band were from 6 to 18 inches.

q.p: NWS Green Bay Winter Weather Message
q.t: ...BLIZZARD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL MIDNIGHT CDT SUNDAY NIGHT... WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph will cause whiteout conditions in blowing snow. Significant drifting of the snow is likely. Additional snow accumulations of 8 to 15 inches are expected.

q.p: NWS Green Bay Area Forecast Discussion · update, RDM
q.t: Blizzard conditions are likely near the lake and bay later tonight through at least midday Sunday, so decided to issue a blizzard warning for Door, Kewaunee, Brown, Outagamie, Southern Marinette and Southern Oconto counties.

q.p: NWS Green Bay Area Forecast Discussion · update, RDM
q.t: There is already considerable blowing and drifting snow. 925mb winds are forecast to be near 50 knots later tonight through at least noon Sunday.

q.p: NWS Green Bay Area Forecast Discussion · update, RDM
q.t: Think that roads could become impassable in some of the blizzard warning areas.

lessons: A week out, the same storm looked like rain and snowmelt.
WPC leaned on the slower ECMWF and UKMET, and slow was right.
MOS's top snow category is 8 inches or more. This storm needed a bigger box.
The NAM ran coldest near the ground; the GFS ran warmest.
The forecasters, not the models, issued the warnings.
